rounds.text: Radha Madhav Corporation Ltd is currently priced at a modest ₹ 2.00 per share with a total market capitalisation of just ₹ 18.3 Cr [E1, E2]. Despite a sharp contraction in trailing twelve-month sales [E6], the business demonstrates an underlying capacity for profitability over medium-term timeframes [E8]. Specifically, the company has achieved a compounded profit growth of 26% over 3 years, alongside a 14% compounded profit growth over 5 years [E8, E7]. This multi-year expansion in earnings reveals operational resilience and an ability to generate value that is obscured by near-term volatility [E8, E7]. Conceded: [E3], [E4], [E5], and [E6].

Radha Madhav Corporation Ltd trades at an extreme and indefensible price-to-book multiple of 16.67x despite its book value standing at a mere ₹ 0.12 [E1]. This lofty valuation is completely detached from the fundamental reality that the company destroys shareholder capital, evidenced by a dismal return on equity of -30.5% and a negative return on capital employed of -8.5% [E5, E4]. Furthermore, the business is failing to generate any top-line momentum, demonstrated by a catastrophic compounded sales growth rate of -100% over the trailing twelve months [E6]. Investors are also receiving zero income for taking on these severe operational risks, as the dividend yield is flat at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: compounded profit growth reached 14% over 5 years and 26% over 3 years [E7, E8].

Conceded: [E1], [E4], [E5], [E6], and [E3]. Despite the backward-looking distress highlighted in those metrics, the bear completely overlooks the actual earnings velocity that the market is beginning to reprice [E2]. The business has actively expanded its bottom-line capacity over medium-term horizons, achieving a 14% compounded profit growth rate over 5 years [E7]. More importantly, that profit acceleration is actively compounding and improving, surging to a 26% compounded profit growth rate over 3 years [E8]. This persistent multi-year profit expansion proves the underlying earnings power of the ₹ 18.3 Cr market capitalisation company far outweighs the static, distorted asset measurements cited by the bear [E2, E8].

Conceded: [E7] and [E8]. While the bull points to multi-year profit acceleration of 14% over 5 years [E7] and 26% over 3 years [E8], this backward-looking profit expansion is entirely disconnected from current operational reality given that compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has collapsed by -100% [E6]. This total evaporation of top-line revenue utterly invalidates the idea of an ongoing earnings velocity, proving that the ₹ 18.3 Cr market capitalisation [E2] is pricing in growth that no longer exists in the business. Furthermore, paying a heavy 16.67x price-to-book multiple on a minuscule book value of ₹ 0.12 [E1] for a company suffering from a catastrophic -30.5% ROE [E5] and a -8.5% ROCE [E4] exposes shareholders to severe capital destruction. The bull's reliance on isolated percentage profit metrics [E7, E8] ignores the glaring reality that the company generates a dividend yield of zero [E3] while bleeding fundamental returns on capital [E4, E5].
